body.statement:
With the Gaussian release noises set to zero and the privacy constraint removed, the constrained optimization actually satisfies, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \inf_{\substack{h\le r_0,\ 1\le k\le m h^d\\
                  m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)}}
 \{B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\}
 \asymp r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee n^{-q/d}.
\]
Thus it equals the advertised KBRW rate precisely in the regimes in which \(r_{\mathrm{np}}\gtrsim n^{-q/d}\); in the low-smoothness regime where the reverse inequality holds, the frozen rank cap forces the additional approximation floor \(n^{-q/d}\).
body.justification: The construction must collapse to the established privacy-free higher-order CATE rate in the standard special case.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 establishes this rate for point estimation; this proposition verifies that the bias-aware interval radius preserves it on the attainable submodel.
body.consumer: Analysts can recover the nonprivate pointwise benchmark continuously as confidentiality constraints are removed.
body.proof_tex:
Again put \(\ell=h k^{-1/d}\).  The constraint \(k\le m h^d\) gives \(\ell\ge m^{-1/d}\), and therefore every admissible choice obeys
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)\gtrsim \ell^q\gtrsim n^{-q/d}.
\]
The same objective also dominates
\[
 h^\gamma+n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}
\]
and hence its infimum is at least
\(r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\).  Finally it dominates, up to fixed factors,
\[
 h^\gamma+\ell^q+n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}.
\]
If all three summands were smaller than \(t\), then
\(h<t^{1/\gamma}\), \(\ell<t^{1/q}\), and the last summand would exceed
\(n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}\).  Balancing this expression with \(t\) proves the lower bound
\[
 r_2=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q))}.
\]
The elbow in the definition of \(r_{\mathrm{np}}\) is exactly the solution of \(r_o=r_2\), so \(r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2\).  This proves the asserted lower bound.

For the reverse inequality set
\(T=r_o\vee r_2\vee n^{-q/d}\).  If \(q<\gamma\), take
\(h=T^{1/\gamma}\), \(\ell=T^{1/q}\), and round
\(k=(h/\ell)^d\) to a positive integer.  The term \(n^{-q/d}\) ensures \(\ell\gtrsim m^{-1/d}\), hence \(k\le m h^d\), and \(r_o,r_2\le T\) give
\[
 n^{-1/2}h^{-d/2}\le T,
 \qquad
 n^{-1}h^{-d/2}\ell^{-d/2}\le T.
\]
The two leading biases equal \(T\), while
\(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\le h^\gamma=T\).  If \(q\ge\gamma\), take \(k=1\) and \(h=T^{1/\gamma}\); then \(h^q\le h^\gamma=T\), and the second sampling term is the square of the first and is smaller for large \(n\).  In both cases the local-sample and boundary constraints hold for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Integer rounding and \(m\asymp n\) alter only constants.  This proves the matching upper bound and the claimed characterization.
